titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Crucifixion and Resurrection in the Prophets (ch. 109–110)
part: ch. 109–110 — the crucifixion and resurrection in the prophets
about: These two short chapters continue the author's proof from the prophets: ch. 109 gathers what Moses, David, Isaiah, Solomon, Jeremiah and Zechariah said about Christ's crucifixion (Psalm 22 and 69, Isaiah 53, the speech of the wicked in the Wisdom of Solomon, Proverbs 1, the thirty pieces of silver, Zechariah 12:10), and ch. 110 does the same for the resurrection (Psalms 12, 82, 44, 68, 78 and 16, Isaiah 53 again, and Solomon's sun). Each citation is introduced by 'and as X prophesied, he said'. The quotations are the author's own wording, so the notes name a source only where the passage is clear and flag the doubtful words with (?). Dillmann's lexicon was not available for this draft.

sentences.t: ፻፱ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ስቅለቱ ።
sentences.l: 109. Concerning crucifixion-his.
sentences.i: Chapter 109: Concerning his crucifixion
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፱ is the numeral 109 (፻ hundred, ፱ nine). በእንተ 'concerning' takes ስቅለቱ, ስቅለት 'crucifixion, hanging' (from ሰቀለ 'hang, crucify') with -ሁ 'his' (ስቅለት + ሁ is written ስቅለቱ: the ት and the suffix merge). The chapter is a catena of prophecies, each opened by the frame ወበከመ ተነበየ X ወይቤ 'and as X prophesied, he said'; the author's wording often fits the quotation to his purpose, and the notes say where I can name a source.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበዩ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ በእንተ ፡ ስቅለቱ ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ቊልዔሁ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ትሬእዩ ፡ መድኀኒትክሙ ፡ ስቁለ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ዕፅ ፡ ወኢተአምኑ ፡ ቦቱ ።
sentences.l: And-again prophesied prophets concerning crucifixion-his for-Christ, and-as prophesied Moses servant(?)-his for-God and-said: 'You-will-see saviour-your hanged upon wood, and-not you-believe in-him.'
sentences.i: And again the prophets prophesied concerning the crucifixion of Christ; and as Moses, the servant(?) of God, prophesied, he said: 'You will see your saviour hanged upon wood, and you will not believe in him.'
sentences.n: ወካዕበ 'and again' (ወ- + ካዕበ). ተነበዩ is the tä-stem perfect of ነበየ, 'they prophesied' (3mp); ተነበየ 'he prophesied' (3ms). ለክርስቶስ: ስቅለቱ takes -ሁ 'his' and ለ- names the possessor afterwards ('his crucifixion, Christ's'). ቊልዔሁ 'his servant' (ቊልዔ with -ሁ; I take it as 'servant, attendant', unconfirmed, since Dillmann was not available (?)); ለእግዚኣብሔር 'of God' by the same ለ- pattern. The saying itself: ትሬእዩ is 2mp imperfect of ርእየ 'see'; ስቁለ is the passive participle 'hanged', in the accusative after the verb; ዲበ ዕፅ 'upon wood' (ዕፅ is also 'tree'; here the wood of the cross). ቦቱ is በ + -ቱ 'in him', after ተአምኑ 'believe'. I cannot match the words to a verse; they perhaps echo Deuteronomy 28:66 about life 'hanging' before the eyes (?). The same frame ወበከመ ተነበየ returns throughout.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወይቤ ፡ አኀዙኒ ፡ ከለባት ፡ ብዙኃን ፡ ወቀነዉኒ ፡ እደዊየ ፡ ወእገርየ ፡ ወኆለቁ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ አዕፅምትየ ፡ እሙንቱሰ ፡ ጠዪቆሙ ፡ ተዐወሩኒ ፡ ወተካፈሉ ፡ አልባስየ ፡ ለርእሶሙ ፡ ወተዓፀዉ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ዐራዝየ ።
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David and-said: 'Seized-me dogs many, and-pierced-me hands-my and-feet-my, and-counted all bones-my; they-indeed, looking, gazed(?)-at-me, and-shared garments-my for-themselves, and-cast-lots(?) upon robe-my.'
sentences.i: And as David prophesied, he said: 'Many dogs have seized me, and they have pierced my hands and my feet, and counted all my bones; as for them, they looked on and gazed(?) at me, and they shared out my garments among themselves, and cast lots(?) over my robe.'
sentences.n: Psalm 22:16–18 (21:17–19 in the Greek numbering): the dogs, the pierced hands and feet, the counted bones, the garments divided, the lot cast. አኀዙኒ is አኀዘ 'seize' (3mp perfect) + -ኒ 'me'; ቀነዉኒ 'they pierced me' (ቀነወ, which I read as 'pierce, bore through' (?)); the objects እደዊየ ወእገርየ 'my hands and my feet' (-የ '1cs my') are accusative. ኆለቁ is 3mp perfect of ኈለቈ 'count'. እሙንቱሰ 'they indeed' (3mp pronoun + emphatic -ሰ) turns to the onlookers; ጠዪቆሙ is a gerund 'looking' (?), and ተዐወሩኒ 'they gazed at me' is a guess (?): the only sense I know for the root ዐወረ is 'be blind' (ዕዉር), which does not fit 'gaze', so the true sense may differ (Dillmann was not available). ተካፈሉ 'they divided among themselves' (reciprocal tä-stem of ከፈለ 'divide'), ለርእሶሙ 'for themselves' (ርእስ 'head' used as 'self'). ተዓፀዉ 'they cast lots' follows the earlier glossary's guess (?); ዐራዝ I take as a garment, 'robe' (?).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ትስብእቱ ፡ ወስቅለቱ ፡ ለክርስቶስ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ መኑ ፡ የአምነነ ፡ ቃልነ ፡ ወለመኑ ፡ ተከሥተ ፡ መዝራዕተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Isaiah prophet concerning incarnation-his and-crucifixion-his for-Christ and-said: 'O-Lord, who believes-us, our-word? And-to-whom was-revealed arm-of God?
sentences.i: And as Isaiah the prophet prophesied concerning the incarnation and the crucifixion of Christ, he said: 'O Lord, who believes our word? And to whom was the arm of God revealed?
sentences.n: Isaiah 53:1. ትስብእት is 'becoming human, incarnation' (from ሰብእ 'human being'), here with -ሁ 'his'. እግዚኦ 'O Lord' is the vocative of እግዚእ. መኑ 'who?'; የአምነነ is the imperfect of አምነ 'believe' with -ነ 'us' and the noun ቃልነ 'our word' in apposition, so 'who believes us, our word' (the Geʿez has both 'us' and 'our word'; the English keeps only the word). ወለመኑ 'and to whom'. ተከሥተ is the passive 'was revealed' (tä-stem of ከሠተ 'open, reveal'), and its subject is መዝራዕተ እግዚኣብሔር 'the arm of God': መዝራዕተ is the construct state (a feminine noun in -ት ends in -ተ before the noun that follows), not a loose accusative. The unit ends at a ፤ with the quotation still open.

sentences.t: ወነገርነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሕፃን ፡ በቅድሜሁ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ሥርው ፡ በውስተ ፡ ምድር ፡ ጽምእት ፡ አልቦ ፡ ላሕየ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ራእየ ፡ ወራእዩሂ ፡ ምኑን ፡ ወትሑት ፡ እምኵሉ ፡ ሰብእ ፤
sentences.l: And-we-told: like child before-him, and-like root in-the-land dry; there-is-not beauty(?) and-there-is-not appearance, and-appearance-his despised and-humble beyond-all men;
sentences.i: We told it: like a child before him, and like a root in a dry land; he had no beauty(?) and no appearance, and his appearance was despised and lowly beyond all men;
sentences.n: Continues Isaiah 53 (verses 2–3). ነገርነ is the perfect of ነገረ 'tell' (1cp 'we told'). ከመ ሕፃን 'like a child'; በቅድሜሁ 'before him' (በ- + ቅድሜ + -ሁ); it may go with ነገርነ ('we told before him') or with the simile, and I keep the Geʿez order. ሥርው 'root, shoot'; ምድር ጽምእት 'a dry land' (ጽምእት is fem., agreeing with ምድር). አልቦ 'there is not' with ላሕየ and ራእየ in the accusative; ላሕይ 'beauty' is not certain (?). ወራእዩሂ is ራእዩ 'his appearance' (ራእይ + -ሁ) + ሂ 'and indeed'. ምኑን is the passive participle 'despised'; ወትሑት 'and humble'; እምኵሉ ሰብእ 'beyond all men' (እም- 'than' used for comparison).

sentences.t: ብእሲሁ ፡ ቅሡፍ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወሕሙም ፡ እስመ ፡ ሜጠ ፡ ገጻ ፡ ወአስተሐቀርዎ ፡ ወኢተሓሰብዎ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ንቅትሎ ፡ ለጻድቅ ፡ እስመ ፡ ክቡድ ፡ ለነ ፡ ይትቃወሞን ፡ ለምግባሪነ ፡ መዝለፌ ፡ ኮነነ ፡ ለኅሊናነ ፡ ወሰቆራረ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ በኀጣውኢነ ፤
sentences.l: his-person scourged is and-sick, for he-turned face, and-they-despised-him and-not they-reckoned-him; and-as prophesied Solomon and-said: 'Let-us-kill the-righteous, for burdensome to-us; he-opposes-us(?), our-works, a-reproach(?) he-became to-us for-our-mind, and-a-reproach(?) became to-him through-our-sins;
sentences.i: his person is scourged and sick, for he turned his face, and they despised him and did not reckon him. And as Solomon prophesied, he said: 'Let us kill the righteous man, for he is a burden to us; he opposes our works(?), he has become a reproach(?) to our mind, and a reproach(?) became to him through our sins;
sentences.n: Isaiah 53:3 closes (ቅሡፍ 'scourged, stricken' and ሕሙም 'sick'; ብእሲሁ 'his person', ብእሲ + -ሁ). ሜጠ ገጻ 'he turned his face': ገጻ is formally ገጽ 'face' + -ሃ 'her' (the accusative would be ገጸ, and 'his' ገጹ); neither fits a masculine subject, so I take it as a slip for 'his face' (?). አስተሐቀርዎ 'they despised him' and ኢተሓሰብዎ 'they did not reckon him' (3mp perfects with -ዎ 'him'). Then Solomon, an echo of the speech of the wicked in the Wisdom of Solomon, chapter 2 (verses 12–20). ንቅትሎ ለጻድቅ: ንቅትሎ is 1cp jussive 'let us kill' + -ኦ 'him' (ንቅትል + ኦ), doubled by ለጻድቅ 'the righteous'. ክቡድ 'heavy, burdensome', ለነ 'to us'. ይትቃወሞን is odd: tä-stem of the III-stem ቃወመ (from ቆመ 'stand'), 'oppose', but the ending -ን matches no suffix I know ('us' would be -ነ); I read 'he opposes us' (?); ለምግባሪነ 'our works' (ምግባር + -ነ). መዝለፌ is a noun 'reproach' (?) (from ዘለፈ 'rebuke'), ኮነነ 'he became to us'. ሰቆራረ I cannot fix (?); 'reproach' is a guess from the parallel, and ሎቱ 'to him' makes the clause obscure. በኀጣውኢነ 'through our sins' (plural of ኀጢአት + -ነ). The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ደገመ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ኢያስሕቱከ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ረሲዓን ፡ ለእመ ፡ ይቤሉከ ፡ ነዓ ፡ ምስሌነ ፡ ተሳተፍ ፡ ንድፍን ፡ ደመ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ ወንንሣእ ፡ በርባሮ ፡ ወይኩነነ ፡ አሐደ ፡ ቊናመተ ፡ ለኵልነ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-repeated and-said: 'My-son, may-they-not-lead-you-astray, men wicked; if they-say-to-you: Come with-us, take-part; let-us-hide blood innocent, and-let-us-take plunder(?), and-let-it-be-for-us one purse(?) for-all-of-us;
sentences.i: And again he repeated, and said: 'My son, let wicked men not lead you astray; if they say to you: Come with us, join us; let us hide innocent blood, and let us take plunder, and let us have one purse(?) for us all;
sentences.n: Proverbs 1:10–14, the invitation of the sinners. ደገመ 'he repeated' (the same speaker, Solomon, speaks again); ወልድየ 'my son' (ወልድ + -የ). ኢያስሕቱከ is the negative jussive of አስሕተ 'lead astray' + -ከ 'you', 'may they not lead you astray'; ሰብእ ረሲዓን 'wicked men' (plural of ረሲዕ). ለእመ ይቤሉከ 'if they say to you'; ነዓ ምስሌነ 'come with us'; ተሳተፍ 'share, take part' (imperative). ንድፍን is 1cp jussive of ደፈነ, which I read as 'cover, hide, bury' (?), with ደመ ንጹሐ 'innocent blood'. በርባሮ I read as 'plunder' (?), unconfirmed; ወይኩነነ 'and let it be for us'; ቊናመተ 'purse' (?), a guess from the sense of a common fund. ለኵልነ 'for all of us' (ኵሉ + -ነ). The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: አግሕሥ ፡ ርእሰከ ፡ እምአሠሮሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ አኮ ፡ በከ ፡ ዘይረብቡ ፡ ለአዕዋፍ ፡ መሥገርተ ።
sentences.l: Withdraw head-your from-their-tracks(?), for not it-is for-you what they-spread(?) for-birds, a-snare.'
sentences.i: Hold your head back from their tracks(?), for it is not for you, what they spread out(?) for the birds: a snare.'
sentences.n: Proverbs 1:15–17. አግሕሥ is the imperative of አግሕሠ, which I read as 'withdraw, hold back' (?). አሠር 'track, trace' (?): the word can also mean a bond, but the sense 'footsteps' suits the saying, though the text says 'head' where one expects 'foot'. አኮ በከ, literally 'not in you / not yours', for 'it is not for you'. ዘይረብቡ 'what they spread (a net)' (ዘ- + imperfect, root r-b-b (?)); ለአዕዋፍ 'for birds' (plural of ዖፍ); መሥገርተ 'snare' in the accusative. The Geʿez is read as it stands.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወወደዩ ፡ ሐሞተ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መብልዕየ ፡ ወአስተዩኒ ፡ ብሒአ ፡ ለጽምእየ ።
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David and-said: 'And-they-put gall into food-my, and-gave-me-to-drink vinegar for-thirst-my.'
sentences.i: And as David prophesied, he said: 'And they put gall into my food, and gave me vinegar to drink for my thirst.'
sentences.n: Psalm 69:21 (68:22 in the Greek numbering), the gall and vinegar of the crucifixion. ወወደዩ 'and they put' (ወደየ, 3mp perfect); ሐሞት 'gall'; መብልዕየ 'my food' (መብልዕ + -የ); ወአስተዩኒ 'and they gave me to drink' (አስተየ, causative of ሰትየ 'drink', + -ኒ 'me'); ብሒአ 'vinegar' (accusative); ለጽምእየ 'for my thirst' (ጽምእ + -የ).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ነሥአ ፡ ደዌነ ፡ ወጾረ ፡ ሕማመነ ፡ ወበቊስለ ፡ ዚአሁ ፡ ሐየውነ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Isaiah prophet and-said: 'He took sickness-our and-bore pain-our, and-by-wound his we-were-healed(lit. lived);
sentences.i: And as Isaiah the prophet prophesied, he said: 'He took our sickness and bore our pain, and by his wound we were healed;
sentences.n: Isaiah 53:4–5. ውእቱ 'he'. ነሥአ 'he took' and ጾረ 'he bore' are 3ms perfects; ደዌነ 'our sickness' and ሕማመነ 'our pain' (ደዌ, ሕማም + -ነ '1cp our'). ወበቊስለ ዚአሁ 'and by his wound' (ዚአሁ is the independent possessive 'of him', the stress on 'his'). ሐየውነ is ሐየወ 'live, be alive' in the 1cp perfect: 'we lived', that is, 'we were restored to life, healed'; 'healed' interprets 'lived' (?). The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወርኢናሁ ፡ ሕሙመ ፡ ወቊሱለ ፡ በሕማም ፡ ወውእቱሰ ፡ ኢከሠተ ፡ አፉሁ ፡ በሕማሙ ፡ ወመጽአ ፡ ይጠባሕ ፡ ከመ ፡ በግዕ ፡ በቅድመ ፡ ዘይቀርጾ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ኢከሠተ ፡ አፉሁ ፡ በሕማሙ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይነሥእዋ ፡ ለነፍሱ ፤
sentences.l: and-we-saw-him sick and-wounded with-pain; and-he-indeed not opened mouth-his in-his-pain, and-came to-be-slaughtered like lamb before him-who-shears-him; likewise not opened mouth-his in-his-pain until they-take it, the-soul-of-him;
sentences.i: and we saw him sick and wounded with pain; yet he did not open his mouth in his pain, and he came to be slaughtered like a lamb before the one who shears it; in the same way he did not open his mouth in his pain until they took his soul;
sentences.n: Isaiah 53:3, 7. ወርኢናሁ 'and we saw him' (ርኢነ 'we saw' + -ሁ). ሕሙመ ወቊሱለ 'sick and wounded' are accusatives of condition. ወውእቱሰ 'and he for his part'. ኢከሠተ አፉሁ 'he did not open his mouth' (አፍ 'mouth', አፉሁ 'his mouth'). ወመጽአ ይጠባሕ 'and he came to be slaughtered' (ይጠባሕ looks like an active imperfect of ጠብሐ 'slaughter'; the sense needs 'to be slaughtered', which I take (?); after a verb of coming it gives the purpose). ከመ በግዕ 'like a lamb'. ዘይቀርጾ is ዘ- + imperfect of ቀረጸ + -ኦ 'him/it', 'he who shears (carves?) it'; 'shears' is my reading (?). ከማሁ 'likewise'. እስከ ይነሥእዋ ለነፍሱ: ነፍስ is fem., so the suffix -ዋ 'her/it' is doubled by ለነፍሱ 'his soul'; 'until they take his soul'. Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወኢየአምርዋ ፡ ለልደቱ ፤
sentences.l: and-not they-know-it, birth-his;
sentences.i: and they will not know his birth;
sentences.n: Isaiah 53:8 in the shape the author gives it. ኢየአምርዋ is the negative imperfect of አእመረ 'know' with the fem. suffix -ዋ 'it', doubled by ለልደቱ 'his birth' (ልደት is fem., from ወለደ 'bear'). A short unit, cut at its ፤ because the speaker changes in the next.

sentences.t: በኀጢአተ ፡ ሕዝብየ ፡ በጻሕኩ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለሞት ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኤርምያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወነሣኡ ፡ ሤጦ ፡ ለክቡር ፡ ፴ ፡ ብሩረ ፡ ዘአክበርዎ ፡ እምደቂቀ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወይቤለኒ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ደዮ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሕንቅርት ፡ ወፍትኖ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ ወወህብዎ ፡ ለገራህተ ፡ ለብሓዊ ፤
sentences.l: For-the-sin of-my-people I-reached unto death. And-as prophesied Jeremiah prophet and-said: 'And-they-took price-his of-the-precious thirty silver, whom they-honoured from sons-of Israel; and-said-to-me God: Put-it into the-treasury(?), and-test-it whether it-be pure, and-give-it to the-smelters(?) for-fire;
sentences.i: On account of the sin of my people I have come as far as death. And as Jeremiah the prophet prophesied, he said: 'And they took the price of the precious one, thirty (pieces) of silver, him whom they valued, from the sons of Israel; and God said to me: Put it into the treasury(?), and test it whether it is pure, and give it to the smelters(?) for the fire;
sentences.n: The first clause continues Isaiah 53 (the speaker's 'I' is the Lord's, in the author's wording); በ- 'on account of'; በጻሕኩ is 1cs perfect of በጽሐ 'arrive, reach'; እስከ ለሞት 'as far as death'. Then Jeremiah: the quotation is the one Matthew 27:9–10 gives to Jeremiah and the Hebrew book of Zechariah has at 11:12–13 (the thirty pieces of silver), shaped here by the author. ፴ is the numeral thirty (spoken ሠላሳ, śäläsa, as the glossary decides); ብሩረ 'silver', accusative. ሤጦ is ሤጥ 'price', accusative, with -ሁ 'his'; ለክቡር 'of the precious one' (ክቡር 'precious, honoured'). ዘአክበርዎ: ዘ- + 'they honoured' (አክበረ 'honour, value') + -ዎ, 'whom they valued'; እምደቂቀ እስራኤል 'from the sons of Israel' (እም- 'from', perhaps 'some of them'; the Geʿez does not say who the valuers were). ወይቤለኒ 'and he said to me'. ደዮ 'put it' (imperative of ወደየ + -ኦ). ሕንቅርት I take as 'treasury' (?), unconfirmed; since the next words say 'test it … for the fire', a smelting vessel, 'crucible', is as likely (?). ፍትኖ 'test it' (ፈተነ). ለእመ ኮነ ንጹሐ 'whether it is pure'. ወወህብዎ 'and give it' (imperative of ወሀበ, plural); ገራህተ 'smelters' (?) is a guess from the context (testing, fire); I half-remember ገራህት as 'field, farmland', which would change the clause, and I cannot settle it without Dillmann (?). Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ አዘዘኒ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እንብብ ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ኆለቊዎ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ኃጥኣን ፡ ወአግብእዎ ፡ ለሞት ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ በዝኁ ፡ እለ ፡ ይጸልኡኒ ፡ በዐመፃ ፡ ወፈደዩኒ ፡ እኪተ ፡ ህየንተ ፡ ሠናይት ፡ ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዘካርያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወሀለዎሙ ፡ ይርአይዎ ፡ ለዘሰቀልዎ ፡ ወወግእዎ ፨
sentences.l: As commanded-me God, I-speak. And-as prophesied Isaiah prophet and-said: 'They-counted-him with sinners, and-delivered-him to-death.' And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'They-multiplied, those-who hate-me in-injustice, and-repaid-me evil in-place-of good.' And-as prophesied Zechariah prophet and-said: 'And-it-is-for-them that-they-see him-whom they-hanged and-pierced.'
sentences.i: As God commanded me, I speak. And as Isaiah the prophet prophesied, he said: 'They counted him with sinners, and they delivered him to death.' And as David the prophet prophesied, he said: 'Those who hate me wrongfully have multiplied, and they repaid me evil in place of good.' And as Zechariah the prophet prophesied, he said: 'They are to see him whom they hanged and pierced.'
sentences.n: This unit holds the end of Jeremiah and three more citations; it is under the length limit of about 45 words, so I did not cut it. በከመ አዘዘኒ እግዚኣብሔር እንብብ: 'as God commanded me' (አዘዘ 'command' + -ኒ) with እንብብ, 1cs imperfect of ነበበ 'speak, say', so 'I speak'. Isaiah 53:12 (and 53:8): ኆለቊዎ 'they counted him' (ኈለቈ), ምስለ ኃጥኣን 'with sinners', ወአግብእዎ ለሞት 'and they delivered him to death' (አግብአ, causative of ገብአ 'return', here 'hand over'). David: Psalm 35:19 and 38:19–20 (or 109:3–5), loosely (?); በዝኁ 'they were many' (በዝኀ), እለ ይጸልኡኒ 'those who hate me'; በዐመፃ 'in injustice'; ፈደዩኒ 'they repaid me' (ፈደየ); ህየንተ ሠናይት 'in place of good' (ሠናይት, fem. 'good'). Zechariah 12:10, the passage John 19:37 uses: ሀለዎሙ 'it is for them, they are to' + ይርአይዎ 'they see him'; ለዘሰቀልዎ is the object marker ለ- + ዘ- 'who' + ሰቀልዎ 'they hung him' (the verb of the cross), ወወግእዎ 'and they pierced him'. The ፨ ends the section.

sentences.t: ወብዙኀ ፡ ዘእምተነግረ ፡ ወተዘመረ ፡ ትንቢተ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ በእንተ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ ወስቅለቱ ፡ ወሞቱ ፡ ወትንሣኤሁ ፡ ወዕርገቱ ፡ ወዳግም ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ በስብሐት ፤
sentences.l: And-much, of-what was-told and-was-sung, prophecy-of prophets concerning his-coming and-his-crucifixion and-his-death and-his-resurrection and-his-ascension and-his-second coming in-glory;
sentences.i: And much of what was told and sung the prophecy of the prophets, about his coming and his crucifixion and his death and his resurrection and his ascension and his second coming in glory;
sentences.n: The author steps back from the quotations. ወብዙኀ is accusative of ብዙኅ 'many, much', used as a noun; ዘእምተነግረ is ዘ- 'that' + እም- 'from' + ተነግረ 'was told' (passive of ነገረ), 'of what was told'; ወተዘመረ 'and was sung' (tä-stem of ዘመረ, 'sing psalms', so the psalms are in view). ትንቢተ ነቢያት 'prophecy of the prophets', in apposition, with ትንቢት in the construct. The clause has no verb of its own; the next unit takes up the same prophecy ('but we recalled little of it'), and the English leaves it hanging as the Geʿez does. Then six nouns each with -ሁ 'his': ምጽአት 'coming', ስቅለት, ሞት 'death', ትንሣኤ 'resurrection' (from ተንሥአ 'arise'), ዕርገት 'ascension', and ዳግም ምጽአቱ 'his second coming' (ዳግም 'second, again'). በስብሐት 'in glory'. The unit ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ ኅዳጠ ፡ ዘከርነ ፡ ትንቢተ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ለእለ ፡ ትሰምዑ ፡ ወተአምኑ ፡ ወትሌብዉ ፡ ንሕነ ፡ በበ፩፩ ፡ ዘከርነ ፤
sentences.l: But-little we-recalled prophecy-of prophets for-those you-hear and-believe and-understand; we, each-one, we-recalled;
sentences.i: But we have recalled little of the prophecy of the prophets, for you who hear and believe and understand; we have recalled each one in turn;
sentences.n: ወባሕቱ 'but'. ኅዳጠ 'little' (accusative of ኅዳጥ, adverbial). ዘከርነ 'we recalled, mentioned' (ዘከረ 'remember, mention'). ለእለ 'for those who' addressing the readers, then the 2mp imperfects ትሰምዑ 'you hear', ተአምኑ 'you believe', ትሌብዉ 'you understand' (ለበወ), the last with -ዉ. በበ፩፩ is the distributive በበ- 'each' with the numeral ፩፩ (one-one): 'one by one'. The first-person plural is the author's own; 'we' for himself and the compilers is not certain (?). Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ተብህለ ፡ በሐዋርያት ፡ በወንጌል ፡ መራሕከነ ፡ ወበነቢያት ፡ ናዘዝከነ ፤
sentences.l: As it-was-said by-the-apostles in-the-gospel, you-guided-us, and-by-the-prophets you-comforted(?)-us;
sentences.i: As it was said by the apostles in the gospel, you guided us, and by the prophets you comforted(?) us;
sentences.n: በከመ ተብህለ 'as it was said' (ተብህለ, passive of ብህለ 'say'). በሐዋርያት 'by the apostles', በወንጌል 'in the gospel'. መራሕከነ and ናዘዝከነ end in -ከነ: 2ms perfect -ከ with -ነ 'us', so 'you guided us', 'you comforted/charged us'. It reads as address to Christ (or God), a doxological turn, and I take it so (?). ናዘዘ 'comfort' is how I read the verb (?); 'charged' from አዘዘ 'command' would, as far as I can tell, not give this shape (?). Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ነገረ ፡ ነቢያት ፡ ያረትዕ ፡ ሃይማኖተ ፡ ኑፉቃን ፨
sentences.l: for word-of prophets makes-straight faith-of the-steadfast(?).
sentences.i: for the word of the prophets sets right the faith of the steadfast(?).
sentences.n: እስመ 'for'. ነገረ ነቢያት 'the word of the prophets' (ነገረ, construct of ነገር). ያረትዕ is the imperfect of አርትዐ 'make straight, set right, confirm'. ሃይማኖተ ኑፉቃን: ሃይማኖት 'faith' in the construct; ኑፉቃን, plural of a word I cannot place (Dillmann was not available) (?): 'steadfast, devout' is only a guess from a root ነፍቀ that I could not check, and the sense might even run the other way. The ፨ closes the chapter.

sentences.t: ፻፲ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ትንሣኤሁ ።
sentences.l: 110. Concerning resurrection-his.
sentences.i: Chapter 110: Concerning his resurrection
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፲ is the numeral 110 (፻ hundred, ፲ ten). ትንሣኤሁ 'his resurrection': ትንሣኤ, from ተንሥአ 'arise', with -ሁ 'his'. The chapter is the same chain of citations as the last, now for the rising.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ትንሣኤሁ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ይእዜ ፡ እትነሣእ ፡ ይቤ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እሬሲ ፡ መድኀኒተ ፡ ወኣግህድ ፡ ቦቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-again concerning resurrection-his prophesied David and-said: 'Now I-shall-arise, says God; I-shall-set salvation, and-I-shall-act-openly(?) in-him;
sentences.i: And again David prophesied concerning his resurrection, and said: 'Now I shall arise, says God; I shall set salvation, and I shall act openly(?) in him;
sentences.n: Psalm 12:5 (11:6 in the Greek numbering). ይእዜ 'now'; እትነሣእ is the 1cs imperfect of ተንሥአ 'arise'; ይቤ እግዚኣብሔር 'God says' (the same ይቤ 'he said', used for a present saying). እሬሲ is the 1cs imperfect of ረሰየ 'set, make'; መድኀኒተ 'salvation, a saviour', accusative, and which of the two senses the author means is not clear. ወኣግህድ is ወ- + the 1cs imperfect of the causative (አግሀደ 'make manifest', from ገሀደ 'be open, manifest'; ኣ is the spelling of its first syllable), so literally 'and I shall make manifest'; ቦቱ 'in him/it'. I read it as 'act openly', with 'show myself in him' as the other reading (?). Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤ ፡ ተንሥእ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ወኰንና ፡ ለምድር ፡ እስመ ፡ አንተ ፡ ትወርስ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ አሕዛብ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said: 'Arise, O-Lord, and-judge-her, the-earth, for you will-inherit among-all nations;
sentences.i: And again he said: 'Arise, O Lord, and judge the earth, for you shall inherit among all the nations;
sentences.n: Psalm 82:8 (81:8 in the Greek numbering). ተንሥእ is the imperative 'arise'; ወኰንና 'and judge' (imperative of ኰነነ 'judge', 2ms ኰንን, with -ኣ 'her', the earth being fem.); ለምድር 'the earth' (ለ- doubling the object -ኣ on the verb); ትወርስ 'you will inherit' (ወረሰ); በኵሉ አሕዛብ 'among all nations'. Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ተንሥእ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ርድአነ ፡ ወአድኅነነ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ስምከ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-prophesied and-said: 'Arise, O-Lord, help-us and-save-us for the-sake-of name-your;
sentences.i: And again he prophesied, and said: 'Arise, O Lord, help us and save us for the sake of your name;
sentences.n: Psalm 44:26 (43:27 in the Greek numbering). ርድአነ 'help us' and ወአድኅነነ 'and save us' are imperatives with -ነ 'us' (ረድአ, አድኀነ). በእንተ ስምከ 'for the sake of your name' (the sense of በእንተ here is 'on account of', not 'concerning'). Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወደገመ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ይትነሣእ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይዘረዉ ፡ ፀሩ ፡ ወይጒየዩ ፡ ጸላእቱ ፡ እምቅድመ ፡ ገጹ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-repeated and-said: 'Let-God-arise, and-let-be-scattered his-enemy, and-let-flee his-haters from-before face-his;
sentences.i: And he repeated, and said: 'Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered, and let those who hate him flee from before his face;
sentences.n: Psalm 68:1 (67:2 in the Greek numbering). ይትነሣእ 'let him arise' (jussive of ተንሥአ); ይዘረዉ 'let them be scattered' (ዘረወ, 3mp jussive); ፀሩ 'his enemy' (ፀር + -ሁ), collective; ይጒየዩ 'let them flee' (ጐየየ); ጸላእቱ 'his haters, foes' (plural ጸላእት + -ሁ); እምቅድመ ገጹ 'from before his face'. ደገመ 'he repeated' marks another quotation by the same speaker. Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወተንሥአ ፡ እግዚአብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘንቃህ ፡ እምንዋም ፡ ወከመ ፡ ኀያል ፡ ወኅዳገ ፡ ወይን ።
sentences.l: And-again he-prophesied and-said: 'And-arose God like one-who awoke from-sleep, and-like a-mighty-man, and-one-who-left(?) wine.'
sentences.i: And again he prophesied, and said: 'And God arose like one who has awakened from sleep, and like a mighty man, and one who has left wine behind(?).'
sentences.n: Psalm 78:65 (77:65 in the Greek numbering). Note the spelling እግዚአብሔር here, with አ where the rest of the part has ኣ; the word is the same, so the glossary keys differ only by the sign. ተንሥአ 'he arose' (perfect, the tense of the psalm); ከመ ዘንቃህ 'like one who awoke' (ዘ- + ንቃህ, a form of ነቅሀ 'wake'; the exact form, perfect or participle, is uncertain (?)); እምንዋም 'from sleep'; ኀያል 'strong, mighty'; ኅዳገ ወይን: ኅዳገ is the accusative of ኅዳግ (from ኀደገ 'leave'), a noun of action, here 'one who leaves'; I read 'one who has left wine behind' (?).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ኢሳይያስ ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ያእትት ፡ ሕማመ ፡ እምነፍሱ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኢገብረ ፡ ኀጢአተ ፡ ወኢተረክበ ፡ ሐሰት ፡ ውስተ ፡ አፉሁ ፤
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Isaiah prophet: 'He-will-remove pain from-his-soul, for not he-did sin, and-not was-found falsehood in his-mouth;
sentences.i: And as Isaiah the prophet prophesied: 'He will remove the pain from his soul, for he did no sin, and no falsehood was found in his mouth;
sentences.n: Isaiah 53:9 and 53:11. This frame has no ወይቤ 'and he said'; the quotation follows ነቢይ directly. ያእትት is the imperfect of አእተተ 'remove, take away' (?); ሕማመ 'pain', accusative; እምነፍሱ 'from his soul' (እም- + ነፍስ + -ሁ). እስመ ኢገብረ ኀጢአተ 'for he did not do sin' (ገብረ 'do'); ወኢተረክበ ሐሰት 'and falsehood was not found' (ተረክበ, passive of ረከበ 'find'); ውስተ አፉሁ 'in his mouth'. Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: ወያርእዮ ፡ ብርሃነ ፡ ወያጸድቆ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ይትቀነይ ፡ ለጽድቅ ፡ ወለሠናይ ፡ ወለብዙኃን ፡ ኀጢአቶሙ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ይደመስስ ፤
sentences.l: and-he-will-show-him light, and-justify-him, for-the-one-who serves for-justice and-for-good; and-for-the-many, their-sins he will-wipe-out;
sentences.i: and he will show him light, and justify him, who serves justice and goodness; and as for the many, he will wipe out their sins;
sentences.n: Isaiah 53:11. ወያርእዮ 'and he will show him' (አርአየ, causative of ርእየ 'see', + -ኦ 'him'), with ብርሃነ 'light', accusative. ወያጸድቆ 'and he will justify him' (አጽደቀ + -ኦ). ለዘ ይትቀነይ ለጽድቅ: ለ- (doubling the object -ኦ) + ዘ + imperfect tä-stem of ቀነየ 'serve': 'him, the one who serves justice'; ጽድቅ 'justice, righteousness', ሠናይ 'good'. ለብዙኃን 'for the many' stands first and ኀጢአቶሙ 'their sins' is object, with ውእቱ 'he' stressed, so 'as for the many, their sins he will wipe out'; ይደመስስ is the imperfect of ደመሰሰ 'wipe out, destroy'. The Geʿez is read as written. Ends at ፤.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ኢገብረ ፡ ኀጢአተ ፡ ወኢተረክበ ፡ ሐሰት ፡ ውስተ ፡ አፉሁ ።
sentences.l: for not he-did sin, and-not was-found falsehood in his-mouth.
sentences.i: for he did no sin, and no falsehood was found in his mouth.
sentences.n: The same words as in unit 24 (Isaiah 53:9), repeated to close the quotation; the repeat is in the source text.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ነቢይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኢተኀድጋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሲኦል ፡ ለነፍስየ ።
sentences.l: And-as prophesied David prophet and-said: 'For you-will-not-leave-her into Sheol, the-soul-of-mine.'
sentences.i: And as David the prophet prophesied, he said: 'For you will not leave my soul in Sheol.'
sentences.n: Psalm 16:10 (15:10 in the Greek numbering), the verse the book of Acts applies to the resurrection. ኢተኀድጋ is the negative imperfect 2ms of ኀደገ 'leave, abandon' with the fem. suffix 'her', doubled by ለነፍስየ 'my soul' (ነፍስ is fem.; -የ 'my'). ውስተ ሲኦል 'into/in Sheol', the netherworld.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ተነበየ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ወልዲ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ወይትሌዐል ፡ ፀሐየ ፡ ጽድቅ ፡ ወይምነ ፡ የዐውድ ፡ ወይገብእ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መካኑ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-as prophesied Solomon his-son and-said: 'And-will-rise(?) the-sun-of righteousness, and-toward-the-south(?) he-circles, and-returns to place-his.' * * *
sentences.i: And as Solomon his son prophesied, he said: 'And the sun of righteousness will rise(?), and he will circle toward the south(?), and return to his place.'
sentences.n: The quotation recalls Ecclesiastes 1:5–6, the sun that rises, circles and returns to its place, with the sun turned into Christ, the sun of righteousness (a title also in Malachi 4:2). ወልዲ is the same form as in ch. 108, taken there and here as 'his son' (David's son), but the ending is unusual and 'my son' is not excluded (?). ይትሌዐል 'he will be raised, rise' (?); ፀሐየ ጽድቅ 'sun of righteousness', construct state; ይምነ I read as 'to the right, southward' (ይምን means right hand and south) (?); የዐውድ 'he goes around' (ዐወደ); ወይገብእ 'and returns' (ገብአ), ውስተ መካኑ 'to his place' (መካን + -ሁ). The final ፨ ፨ ፨ belongs to this unit and ends the part.
